result_text:
`is_ip_allowed` now rejects IPv6 addresses that embed a blocked IPv4 address in any of the listed transition forms. All 8 reject examples return `False`, and all 4 public-embedded examples still return `True`. The SSRF test file passes (43 tests, including the new ones). I didn't run the full suite or `prek`.

The change is in `fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/auth/ssrf.py`. A new helper, `_embedded_ipv4_candidates`, collects every IPv4 address a given IPv6 address could embed:
- IPv4-mapped
- 6to4
- Teredo (server and client)
- NAT64 well-known prefix
- NAT64 local-use prefix (all four RFC 6052 layouts)
- IPv4-translated
- IPv4-compatible (excluding `::` and `::1`)
- ISATAP

`is_ip_allowed` rejects the address if any one candidate is blocked. The existing global-unicast and multicast checks still run first.

I didn't write a separate `validate_url` test. It calls `is_ip_allowed` on resolved IPs, so I expect it to raise `SSRFError` with "blocked IP" for the new forms.

I added parametrized tests in `tests/server/auth/test_ssrf_protection.py` covering the blocked and allowed examples from your description.
